scene_transitions.name: CUT TO
scene_transitions.description: Direct, immediate transition between scenes. The most common transition in screenwriting.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: Use for straightforward scene changes, action sequences, or when you want abrupt shifts in location or time.
scene_transitions.formatting: Right-aligned, all caps, followed by colon
scene_transitions.example:
INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

John sips his espresso, staring out the window.

                                                    CUT TO:

EXT. CITY STREET - DAY

John walks briskly down the sidewalk.
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Creates sense of continuity and forward momentum. Viewers expect immediate connection between scenes.

scene_transitions.name: DISSOLVE TO
scene_transitions.description: Gradual transition where one image fades out while another fades in, suggesting passage of time or emotional connection.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: Use for time passage, dream sequences, flashbacks, or to create emotional resonance between scenes.
scene_transitions.formatting: Right-aligned, all caps, followed by colon
scene_transitions.example:
INT. HOSPITAL ROOM - NIGHT

Sarah holds her father's hand as he sleeps.

                                              DISSOLVE TO:

INT. SAME - MORNING

Sunlight streams through the window. The bed is empty.
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Softens transitions, implies time passing or emotional transformation. More contemplative than CUT TO.

scene_transitions.name: MATCH CUT
scene_transitions.description: Transition using visual similarity between ending of one scene and beginning of next. Highly cinematic.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: Use to draw parallels, show contrast, create metaphors, or make thematic connections between scenes.
scene_transitions.formatting: Often just 'CUT TO:' but relies on visual description to show the match
scene_transitions.example:
INT. DETECTIVE'S OFFICE - DAY

Detective closes a case file folder. The red cover fills the frame.

                                                    CUT TO:

EXT. CRIME SCENE - NIGHT

A red car door slams shut, filling the frame.

[Note: Both scenes feature red object filling frame]
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Creates visual poetry, makes viewers connect ideas, powerful for themes and symbolism.

scene_transitions.name: FADE OUT / FADE IN
scene_transitions.description: Scene gradually fades to black (FADE OUT) then new scene emerges from black (FADE IN). Signals major shift.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: End of acts, major time jumps, to signal 'chapter breaks' in story. FADE OUT is also used at script's end.
scene_transitions.formatting: Right-aligned for FADE OUT, left-aligned for FADE IN
scene_transitions.example:
INT. GRADUATION CEREMONY - DAY

Maria tosses her cap in the air with her classmates.

                                                  FADE OUT.

FADE IN:

INT. CORPORATE OFFICE - DAY - FIVE YEARS LATER

Maria, now in a business suit, leads a meeting.
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Strongest sense of conclusion and new beginning. Gives viewers 'breathing room' between major story sections.

scene_transitions.name: SMASH CUT
scene_transitions.description: Jarring, abrupt transition for shock value or emphasis. Often from calm to chaos or vice versa.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: Use for dramatic reveals, comedy timing, wake-up scenes, or sudden reversals. Sparingly for maximum impact.
scene_transitions.formatting: Right-aligned, all caps, followed by colon. Sometimes written as 'SMASH CUT TO:'
scene_transitions.example:
INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT

Tom lies peacefully in bed, smiling in his sleep.

                                              SMASH CUT TO:

INT. BATTLEFIELD - DAY

EXPLOSIONS everywhere. Tom runs for his life, screaming.
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Jolts the audience, creates contrast, emphasizes sudden change. Comedic or dramatic depending on context.

scene_transitions.name: JUMP CUT
scene_transitions.description: Abrupt cut within same scene, showing time passing or repetitive action. Modern, stylized technique.
scene_transitions.when_to_use: Montages within single location, showing passage of time, repetitive actions, or frenetic pacing.
scene_transitions.formatting: Usually just described in action lines, not explicitly called out
scene_transitions.example:
INT. ARTIST'S STUDIO - DAY

Emma sketches a portrait.

JUMP CUT:

The portrait is more detailed. Light has shifted.

JUMP CUT:

Emma steps back, the portrait nearly complete. Dusk outside.

[Shows time compression within same scene]
scene_transitions.psychological_effect: Disorienting yet rhythmic. Shows progression, builds energy, or creates comic effect.
